Parse the Health Canada Drug Product Database (DPD) Data Extract

Source: R/health_canada_dpd_parser.R
parseHealthCanadaDPD.Rd

Reads Health Canada's Drug Product Database data extract and returns a dvobject with its 13 tables. Each of the four product sets (marketed, approved, cancelled, dormant) is read from its unzipped folder or straight from its zip; the rows of every set go in one table with an extract column.

Usage

parseHealthCanadaDPD(
  dpd_dir,
  extracts = c("marketed", "approved", "cancelled", "dormant"),
  release = NULL,
  release_date = NULL,
  retrieved_at = NULL
)

Arguments

dpd_dir

Character. Folder holding the extract's zips or unzipped folders.

extracts

Character. Product sets to read, any of "marketed", "approved", "cancelled" and "dormant" (all by default).

release

Character or NULL. Release label, e.g. "2026-10". DPD publishes no release number.

release_date

Date, "YYYY-MM-DD" or NULL. Release date.

retrieved_at

Date, "YYYY-MM-DD" or NULL. Date the files were downloaded.

Value

A dvobject with 13 tibbles, each keyed by drug_code: drug_product, active_ingredients, companies, form, packaging, pharmaceutical_std, route, schedule, status, therapeutic_class, veterinary_species, biosimilars (each with extract) and inactive_products. inactive_products lists cancelled products, so it is built only when extracts includes "cancelled" and an inactive products file is found.

Details

dpd_dir holds the extract as Health Canada distributes it, each product set either as its zip or unzipped into a folder of the same name: allfiles (marketed), allfiles_ap (approved), allfiles_ia (cancelled) and allfiles_dr (dormant), plus inactive (the inactive products list). Zips are extracted to a temporary folder that is removed after reading. When neither inactive nor inactive.zip is there, inactive.txt is read from the cancelled set, which holds the same file.

The files have no header: column names are those of Health Canada's read-me ("Read Me File - Drug Product Database (DPD) Data Extract"), lower case, and table names are the read-me's without QRYM_. Every value is quoted and the files are UTF-8; empty values become NA. Code columns (drug_code, active_ingredient_code, company_code, pharm_form_code, route_of_administration_code, si_code) are integers and the DD-MON-YYYY dates are dates; every other column stays text as written. Dates are kept as written, including two lot expiry dates in the cancelled set written with years 0030 and 0031.

The therapeutic class files hold four fields where the read-me lists seven columns: the three certain ones are kept and the parser stops if the fourth ever holds a value.

The parser groups nothing: status holds every status row as written, with current_status_flag marking each product's current one.

DPD data are published under the Open Government Licence - Canada (version 2.0); the attribution it asks for is recorded in the object's metadata (see get_source_metadata). The DPD extract page also links to Health Canada's website terms; the dataset record on open.canada.ca states the Open Government Licence – Canada.

See also

Other parsers: cett_nodes_options(), drug_node_options(), parseDrugBank(), parseHGNC(), parseHPO(), parseOnSIDES(), parseOpenFDA(), parseTWOSIDES(), references_node_options()

Examples

dpd_dir <- system.file("extdata", "health_canada_dpd", package = "dbparser")
dpd <- parseHealthCanadaDPD(dpd_dir, release = "2026-10",
                            retrieved_at = "2026-10-21")
#> Parsed 12 DPD products from marketed, approved, cancelled, dormant.
dpd$drug_product[, c("drug_code", "brand_name", "extract")]
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>    drug_code brand_name                                                  extract
#>        <int> <chr>                                                       <chr>  
#>  1        15 AVENTYL                                                     market…
#>  2        85 ATRAVET 10 MG INJECTABLE                                    market…
#>  3       129 GERME ZONE                                                  market…
#>  4     18349 ASAPHEN                                                     market…
#>  5     81048 OMNITROPE                                                   market…
#>  6     14535 APO-CLOMIPRAMINE                                            approv…
#>  7     99581 NOROMBY                                                     approv…
#>  8         2 ORINASE 0.5GM                                               cancel…
#>  9     80771 MEDROXYPROGESTERONE ACETATE INJECTABLE SUSPENSION USP       cancel…
#> 10     94947 50+ DRY TOUCH CRÈME PROTECTION SOLAIRE LARGE SPECTRE FPS 5… cancel…
#> 11        31 NEO-BEX INJECTABLE                                          dormant
#> 12       126 DEWORMER LIQUID 12.4%                                       dormant
get_source_metadata(dpd)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   metadata_version source          source_name release release_date retrieved_at
#>   <chr>            <chr>           <chr>       <chr>   <date>       <date>      
#> 1 1                health_canada_… Health Can… 2026-10 NA           2026-10-21  
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: source_url <chr>, licence <chr>, licence_url <chr>,
#> #   attribution <chr>, files <list>, parser <chr>
